theater: 珍珠港與西太平洋戰場

battle.name: 太平洋戰爭
battle.theater: 珍珠港與西太平洋戰場
battle.brief: 1941年12月7日珍珠港遭日本偷襲，太平洋戰爭全面爆發，至1945年9月以同盟國勝利告終。卡面的M4A3E8謝爾曼坦克1944年才量產，並未參與珍珠港之役，而在關島、萊伊泰、硫磺島與沖繩的登陸灘頭上陣，用76毫米砲撕開日軍岸防工事與縱深陣地，成為反攻階段最吃重的近距支援兵器。

kit.name: M4A3E8謝爾曼坦克
kit.history: 1944年列裝的美軍中型坦克後期型，配屬太平洋登陸部隊，負責近距火力支援與突破岸防工事。

countries: 太平洋戰爭自1941年12月7日珍珠港遭襲開打，到1945年9月2日日本簽署投降書結束，是第二次世界大戰中航程最遠、戰場最分散的一個戰區，交戰雙方是同盟國與軸心國。同盟國方面由美國扮演主角：1941年12月8日杜魯門總統在珍珠港向國會宣布美軍陣亡，加拿大、澳洲、紐西蘭與英國自治領隨後相繼宣戰；英國以遠東司令部（駐樟宜）承擔初期馬來亞與緬甸戰事，澳洲第九師自中東調回後由蒙哥馬利率領投入；中華民國自1937年起持續抗戰，1941年12月9日加入同盟國，遠征軍入緬作戰；蘇聯於1945年8月8日對日宣戰，蒙古人民共和國同時出兵，由蒙古人民革命軍配合紅軍推進至南千島群島。軸心國方面以日本為核心，1941年12月德國、義大利等國與日本簽署《反共產國際條約》後公開結盟；日本陸軍設南方軍總司令部統轄南方作戰，海軍由聯合艦隊司令長官山本五十六指揮，航空兵力分屬海軍航空隊與陸軍航空兵總司令部。泰國站在日方參戰，昂山率領的緬甸獨立軍在緬北作戰，印度國民軍部分兵力投入安達曼與伊爾瓦底戰線。指揮體系上，同盟國由艾森豪威爾掌國防部、馬歇爾任陸軍參謀長，戰區劃分為西南太平洋（麥克阿瑟）、中部太平洋（尼米茲）與北阿拉斯加至阿留申群島（海軍上將金督導）；日方則運作於大本營、參謀本部與軍令部三段式，戰略計畫集中於參謀，戰術臨場多由中將級指揮官自行決斷。
countriesEn: The Pacific War ran from the Japanese strike on Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941 to the Japanese signature of surrender on 2 September 1945. It was by far the most widely dispersed and the longest-ranging theatre of the Second World War, fought between the Allies and the Axis. On the Allied side the United States played the leading part: on 8 December President Truman addressed Congress and reported the American dead, and Canada, Australia, New Zealand and the British Dominions followed with declarations of war; Britain carried the early Malayan and Burmese fighting through the Far East Command at Singapore, while the Australian 9th Division, pulled back from the Middle East, was led into the theatre by General Sir Thomas Blamey; the Republic of China, which had been resisting Japan since 1937, entered the war on 9 December 1941 and sent the Chinese Expeditionary Force into Burma; the Soviet Union declared war on Japan on 8 August 1945, with the Mongolian People's Republic joining at the same time, the Mongolian People's Revolutionary Army advancing alongside the Red Army to the southern Kuril Islands. On the Axis side Japan was the core: after Germany, Italy and the others adhered to the Tripartite Pact in December 1941, Japan and its partners fought openly as allies. The Japanese Army created the Southern Expeditionary Army Group to command operations in the south, the Navy was led by the Commander-in-Chief of the Combined Fleet, Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto, and air power was split between the Navy Air Service and the Army Air Force. Thailand fought on the Japanese side, the Burma Independence Army under Aung San operated in northern Burma, and elements of the Indian National Army took part in the Andaman and Irrawaddy fighting. The two command systems were entirely different. On the Allied side Dwight Eisenhower chaired the War Department, George Marshall served as Army Chief of Staff, and the theatre was divided into the Southwest Pacific Area under Douglas MacArthur, the Central Pacific Area under Chester Nimitz, and the North Pacific and Aleutians area under Admiral Ernest King of the Pacific Fleet. On the Japanese side decisions ran through the Imperial General Headquarters, the Army and Navy General Staffs, and the Navy's Operations Department: strategy and planning were centralised in the staffs, while tactical command on the spot was left largely in the hands of lieutenant general commanders.
people: 這場戰爭的決策核心是兩位戰區司令、一位參謀長與一位海軍統帥。美國方面，陸軍參謀長喬治·馬歇爾在珍珠港事變後力主歐洲為先、亞洲以海軍與海軍陸戰隊逐步反攻的整體戰略，並以參謀總部協調兩洋兵力的補充與訓練；道格拉斯·麥克阿瑟出任西南太平洋戰區司令，拒絕在初期退守澳洲，主張以登陸反攻保住海軍陸戰隊的訓練體系，其墨爾本之圍保住了澳洲大陸；切斯特·尼米茲接掌中部太平洋戰區，策劃瓜達爾普、馬里安納、萊伊泰、硫磺島與沖繩的兩棲跳島；海軍上將歐內斯特·金任太平洋艦隊與聯合艦隊統帥，雷蒙德·斯普魯恩斯率第五艦隊在珊瑚海、東所羅門、馬里安納與日本海逐步爭取制海權；海軍陸戰隊則由哈爾西在關島、硫磺島與沖繩一線指揮。盟國政治層面有羅斯福、邱吉爾與蔣介石，蔣介石堅持抗戰使日本無法在中國戰場速戰速決。日本方面，1941年7月與9月的兩次御前會議決定南進與對美英開戰，山本五十六以航母機動部隊奇襲珍珠港，卻在中途島遭美軍五分鐘內連續空襲的重創，殘存主力退守本土；東條英機於1941年10月組閣後推動全面開戰，杉山元與永野修身先後擔任陸軍參謀總長與海軍軍令部總長；前線由南方軍總司令寺內幸一、第十六軍司令今村均與南寧海軍司令阿部兼中等中將級指揮官負責；參與珍珠港作戰方案覆核的井本忠晴等人修正了計畫中航線與兵力分配的漏洞。1945年8月日本接受《波茨坦宣言》放棄決戰計畫，最終出自昭和天皇的裁可，與參謀本部放棄本土決戰的轉向同步。
peopleEn: The decision-making core of this war was two theatre commanders, one Army Chief of Staff and one admiral. On the American side George Marshall, Chief of Staff after the Pearl Harbor affair, insisted on Europe first and on a gradual counteroffensive in Asia by the Navy and the Marine Corps, and used the Army General Staff to coordinate the reinforcement and training of forces in both oceans; Douglas MacArthur took command of the Southwest Pacific Area, refused to retire to Australia in the opening months, and pressed for a landing counteroffensive so that the Marine Corps would keep its trained strength, his defence of Melbourne preserving the Australian continent; Chester Nimitz took the Central Pacific and planned the amphibious leap across the islands at Guam, the Marianas, Leyte, Iwo Jima and Okinawa; Admiral Ernest King commanded the Pacific Fleet and the Combined Fleet, while Raymond Spruance led the Fifth Fleet in the Coral Sea, the Eastern Solomons, the Marianas and the Japan Sea, gradually winning the sea; the Marine Corps was led by William Halsey in the Guam, Iwo Jima and Okinawa campaigns. On the political level of the Allies were Roosevelt, Churchill and Chiang Kai-shek, and Chiang's refusal to accept a negotiated settlement kept Japan from ending the war in China. On the Japanese side, two Imperial Conferences in July and September 1941 settled on the southern advance and on war with the United States and Britain; Isoroku Yamamoto struck Pearl Harbor with the carrier strike force, but was mauled at Midway by successive American air attacks, and the surviving core withdrew to the home islands; Hideki Tojo formed a government in October 1941 and pushed the war to the full; Hajime Sugiyama and Yoshiyuki Toyoda served in turn as Army Chief of Staff and Navy Chief of the Naval General Staff, and the front was run by lieutenant generals such as Count Hisaichi Terauchi, General Anami Korechika of the 16th Army and Vice Admiral Abei Kenzō of the Southern Naval Group; staff officers such as Tadayuki Imoto checked and amended the Pearl Harbor plan, closing gaps in its routing and force disposition. In August 1945 Japan abandoned the decisive battle plan and accepted the Potsdam Declaration on the sovereign decision of the Emperor, in step with the General Staff giving up the plan for a final battle on the home islands.
kits: 卡面這輛M4A3E8謝爾曼是1944年才大量裝配的美軍中型坦克後期型，與戰爭開打時日本海軍憑藉戰艦和艦載機偷襲珍珠港的年代相隔數年，牠真正上戰線是在同盟國反攻的島嶼爭奪戰。車上裝76毫米砲與75發砲彈架，乘員五人，汽油引擎配高浮動履帶，最大時速約三十公里，最大行程約二百四十公里，戰備重量約三十二噸，前部裝甲約八十九毫米。1944至1945年間美軍共生產約五千輛，絕大部分配屬裝甲師、海軍陸戰隊與獨立的裝甲旅，在關島突破日軍縱深陣地、萊伊泰內陸的塔克岡戰鬥、硫磺島的坑道與火網陣地，以及沖繩的長岡與首里攻防，都出現了成建制的A3E8群。與之相對的是日本陸軍九七式坦克約三千九百輛，絕大多數只配37毫米甚至更小口徑的短砲，另有數百輛裝甲車與數十門一式砲；登陸雙方還大量使用水陸兩用裝備，包括美軍DUKW、LVT兩棲戰車、LVT(A)裝甲砲車、Lee與Grant登陸坦克，以及LCM、LCVP登陸艇與浮游式爆破小艇；火炮方面是M2 105毫米榴砲、M4突擊砲與37毫米支援砲，另有卡車、裝甲回收車與工程部隊器材。空戰與海戰同樣決定戰局：P-51野馬式、F4U海軍戰鬥機、F6F惡魔式、B-24與B-29壓制日軍航空隊，日本則以零式戰鬥機、一式陸攻與四式中型機迎戰，聯合艦隊的戰列艦、巡洋艦與潛艦在制海權爭奪中消耗殆盡。
kitsEn: The M4A3E8 Sherman on the card is a late model American medium tank that only came into mass production in 1944, several years after the Japanese Navy struck Pearl Harbor with battleships and carrier aircraft; the tank actually reached the fighting line in the island campaigns of the Allied counteroffensive. It carried a 76 mm gun with a 75 round rack, a crew of five, a gasoline engine with high-flotation tracks, a maximum road speed of about thirty kilometres an hour, a range of roughly two hundred and forty kilometres, a combat weight near thirty-two tonnes and frontal armour of about eighty-nine millimetres. Between 1944 and 1945 some five thousand were built, and the great majority went to armoured divisions, Marine Corps units and independent tank battalions; formed groups of A3E8s appear in the breakthrough against the Japanese deep positions at Guam, in the fight for Taykoan in the interior of Leyte, in the tunnel and fire net defences of Iwo Jima, and in the battles of Nagao and Shuri in Okinawa. On the other side of the line, the Japanese Army had about 3,900 Type 97 tanks, the great majority armed with 37 mm or even smaller short guns, together with several hundred armoured cars and a few dozen Type 1 guns. Both amphibious sides relied heavily on wheeled and tracked water-going equipment: the American DUKW, LVT amphibious tractors, LVT(A) gun tractors, Lee and Grant landing tanks, and LCM and LCVP landing craft with small manned demolition boats; artillery included the M2 105 mm howitzer, the M4 assault gun and 37 mm support guns, alongside trucks, armoured recovery vehicles and engineer equipment. Air and sea power decided as much as the ground: the P-51 Mustang, the F4U Corsair, the F6F Hellcat, the B-24 and the B-29 wore down the Japanese air arm, while Japan answered with the Zero fighter, the Type 1 land attack aircraft and the Type 4 medium bomber; the Combined Fleet's battleships, cruisers and submarines were worn down in the struggle for sea control.
tactics: 太平洋戰爭的戰術主軸是兩棲登陸與制空制海權的爭奪。珍珠港一役，日軍以六艘航母組成機動部隊，艦載機分波次攻擊珍珠港與希卡姆機場，並以潛艦封鎖港口對外航道；中途島之戰則是情報作業的示範，美方破譯日軍密碼掌握主攻方向，日方以四艘主力艦換取三座機場，最終折損四艦與逾兩百架飛機。島嶼攻擊有一套固定程序：先由戰艦與巡洋艦實施艦炮射擊，再由航空兵與榴砲兵驅散守軍，兩棲艇與登陸艇在火箭艇、浮游機與蛙人配合下衝灘，建立灘頭堡後由工程兵搶修道路與機場，待後續部隊上岸再實施戰術突破，關島在1944年8月完成第二次突破，硫磺島在1945年3月、沖繩在1945年4月各做一次戰術突破。日軍的守禦依賴灘頭反斜面陣地、縱深坑道與地下機場，靠夜襲與突襲消耗登陸部隊，硫磺島與沖繩的還擊多屬一次性的密集衝鋒，兵器以竹槍、輕機槍與坑道炸藥為主。物流是整場戰爭的勝負手：美軍以潛艦輸送部隊，並用補給船隊在登陸點附近建立近距離後勤區，靠LST卸載、重型艦艇與空投維持島上部隊，麥克阿瑟的原則是登陸部隊一旦上岸就不放棄，寧可海路迂迴也不讓部隊被切斷。
tacticsEn: The tactical spine of the Pacific War was the amphibious landing fought together with the contest for air and sea control. At Pearl Harbor the Japanese formed a strike force of six carriers, flew their aircraft in waves against the harbour and Hickam Field, and used submarines to bottle up the harbour mouth. Midway was a demonstration of intelligence work: American codebreaking had pinned down the Japanese axis of attack, and the Japanese paid for three airfields with four capital ships, finally losing four battleships and more than two hundred aircraft. The assault on an island followed a fixed sequence: naval gunfire from battleships and cruisers first, then bombers and howitzers to drive the defenders off their positions, then landing craft running for the beach under cover of rocket boats, unmanned torpedo craft and frogmen; once the beachhead was consolidated engineers rushed forward to build roads and airfields, and only after the follow-up divisions landed ashore would the tactical breakthrough begin, as at Guam in August 1944, at Iwo Jima in March 1945 and at Okinawa in April 1945. Japanese defence relied on beach defences set on the reverse slope, deep tunnel systems and underground airfields, and on night counterattacks meant to bleed the landing force; the Japanese counterthrusts on Iwo Jima and Okinawa were mostly single massed charges, and their weapons were bamboo spears, light machine guns and demolition charges inside the tunnels. Logistics decided the war: American submarines carried troops forward and supply ships established close support areas near the landing beaches, with LSTs, heavy warships and air drops keeping the island garrisons supplied. MacArthur's rule was that once a landing force was ashore it was never abandoned, and that supply would go the long way round by sea rather than allow the force to be cut off.
data: 幾個常見的統計數字可以標出這場戰爭的規模。珍珠港一役美軍陣亡2,403人、受傷1,178人，5艘受創戰列艦中有3艘當夜沉沒，日軍則損失約29架飛機與1艘潛艦。中途島海戰日軍折損4艘主力艦與約248架飛機，美軍沉1艘航母並損失約150架飛機；珊瑚海海戰雙方各失去1艘主力艦，日本損失約59架、美國約69架飛機。陸戰的殘酷程度逐級上升：瓜達爾普之役日軍約1.7萬人陣亡、1萬人被俘，美軍陣亡約1,782人；萊伊泰之役日軍約3萬人陣亡、1.2萬人被俘，美軍陣亡約1,008人、受傷約2,758人；硫磺島之役美軍1,256人死亡（其中作戰陣亡682人），日軍守軍約1.8萬至2.1萬人幾乎全滅；沖繩之役日軍約9.4萬人陣亡、1.1萬人被俘，美軍4,913人陣亡、3萬餘人受傷，整體而言，美軍在太平洋戰爭陣亡約4萬至5萬人，日軍軍人死亡以百萬計，日本商船損失約880萬噸，約佔戰前船隊總噸位的四成半。
dataEn: A few commonly cited figures mark the scale of this war. At Pearl Harbor the Americans lost 2,403 dead and 1,178 wounded, three of five damaged battleships went down that night, and Japan lost about 29 aircraft and one submarine. At Midway Japan lost four capital ships and roughly 248 aircraft, while the United States lost one carrier and about 150 aircraft; in the Battle of the Coral Sea each side lost a capital ship, Japan about 59 aircraft and the United States about 69. The cost of the land fighting rose step by step: at Guam about 17,000 Japanese were killed and 10,000 taken prisoner, with about 1,782 American dead; at Leyte about 30,000 Japanese were killed and 12,000 captured, with 1,008 Americans dead and about 2,758 wounded; at Iwo Jima 1,256 Americans died, of whom 682 were killed in action, while the Japanese garrison of roughly 18,000 to 21,000 men was almost annihilated; at Okinawa about 94,000 Japanese were killed and 11,000 captured, while 4,913 Americans died and more than 30,000 were wounded. Taken as a whole, American military deaths in the Pacific ran in the range of 40,000 to 50,000, Japanese military deaths ran into the millions, and Japan lost about 8.8 million tons of merchant shipping, close to 45 per cent of the fleet it had possessed before the war.
cause: 日本走向開戰，是資源、戰略時機與中國戰場三重壓力疊加的結果。最直接的導火線是石油：日本帝國的石油儲備在1930年代陸續枯竭，而美國在1940年9月通知終止《美日通商航海條約》之後，日本便失去了在美國購買石油的最後管道，荷屬東印度的婆羅洲油田遂成為南進的首要目標，南進同時也為了取得高品位鋁土礦與橡膠。戰略時機方面，1941年6月德國進攻蘇聯，歐洲戰局驟然改變，參謀本部判斷英美資源將被歐洲吸住，遂在7月2日御前會議上決定南進並準備對蘇開戰，7月28日與9月6日兩次御前會議再通過《帝國國策要綱》與對美英開戰的決定。另一層是中國戰場的泥潭：自1937年全面抗戰以來，日軍未能迫使中國屈服，國民政府仍堅持到底，東條英機的新政府需要一個新戰場來切斷美國援華的通道。日本也計算了兵力對比：海軍航空隊擁有十數艘航母與三百餘架作戰機，認為足以在美軍太平洋艦隊主力尚未集結之前打出一場速決的攻擊，而帝國本土與南方資源的差距又逼著它必須在資源耗盡前取得南方油田。
causeEn: Japan's drift into war was the product of three pressures layered on top of one another: resources, strategic timing and the bogged-down China campaign. The most immediate trigger was oil. The Japanese Empire's oil reserves were used up through the 1930s, and when the United States notified in September 1940 that the American-Japanese Treaty of Commerce and Navigation would be terminated, Japan lost the last channel through which it could buy oil in America. The oil fields of the Dutch East Indies in Borneo therefore became the primary object of the southern advance, which also aimed at high-grade bauxite and rubber. On timing, German attack on the Soviet Union in June 1941 changed the European situation overnight; the Japanese General Staff judged that British and American strength would be absorbed in Europe, and so the Imperial Conference of 2 July resolved on the southern advance and on preparations for war with the Soviet Union, while the conferences of 28 July and 6 September approved the National Defense Policy and the decision for war against the United States and Britain. A third layer was the quagmire of China: since the full-scale war of 1937 the Japanese armies had not forced China to yield, the Nationalist government held out, and the new Tojo government wanted a new theatre in which to cut the American supply line to China. Japan also weighed the balance of forces: the naval air service had a dozen-odd carriers and some three hundred combat aircraft, and the leadership believed it could win a quick decision before the main body of the American Pacific Fleet had gathered, while the gap between the home islands and southern resources pushed the empire to seize the southern oilfields before its reserves ran out.
impact: 太平洋戰爭把美國從歐洲戰場之外的孤立國家推上世界霸主的位子，也重塑了戰後的國際秩序。戰時的美國工業動員創造出自由輪這種量產標準船，總數逾2,700艘，大量運載部隊與物資橫渡太平洋；美軍在馬里安納取得制空權之後，B-24與B-29得以深入日本本土，最終在1945年8月6日與9日投放原子彈，加上蘇聯在8月8日對日宣戰並於8月9日出兵遠東，才迫使日本接受《波茨坦宣言》。制度層面的後果更為長久：1942年1月1日的《聯合國宣言》由26國簽署，1945年6月舊金山會議通過《聯合國憲章》，戰後的國際秩序、安全理事會與戰爭責任的概念都源於此。日本走向相反方向：戰敗後非軍國化並被盟軍佔領，戰後憲法廢除戰爭權力，1951年《舊金山和約》簽訂後才重建國際地位。對亞洲而言，這場戰爭是去殖民化的起點，台灣在1945年10月25日回歸中華民國版圖，朝鮮於同年八月脫離日本統治，越南在1945年八月取得革命勝利，戰後十年間亞洲的殖民地與自治領陸續取得獨立，聯合國的託管制度正是在這樣的背景下設計出來。
impactEn: The Pacific War lifted the United States from the position of an isolated power outside the European theatre to that of a world hegemon, and it reshaped the international order that followed. American industrial mobilisation in wartime produced the Liberty ship, a standardised vessel built in series, with more than 2,700 completed, carrying troops and cargo across the Pacific in bulk. Once the Americans had won air superiority in the Marianas, the B-24 and the B-29 were able to reach deep into the Japanese home islands, and the atomic bombs dropped on 6 and 9 August 1945, together with the Soviet declaration of war on 8 August and the Soviet entry into the Far East on 9 August, forced Japan to accept the Potsdam Declaration. The institutional consequences were longer lived still: the Declaration by United Nations of 1 January 1942 was signed by twenty-six states, and the United Nations Charter was approved at the San Francisco Conference in June 1945; the postwar international order, the Security Council and the very concept of war guilt all trace back to this. Japan went the other way: after defeat it was demilitarised and occupied by the Allies, its new constitution renounced the right to wage war, and it only rebuilt its international position after the San Francisco Peace Treaty of 1951. For Asia the war was the opening of decolonisation. Taiwan returned to the territory of the Republic of China on 25 October 1945, Korea left Japanese rule in August of the same year, Vietnam won its revolution in August 1945, and within a decade the colonies and dominions of Asia gained independence in turn. The trusteeship system of the United Nations was designed in exactly this context.
result: 結果是日本無條件投降，太平洋戰爭以同盟國的完全勝利告終。1945年8月15日，日本政府以天皇詔書宣布接受《波茨坦宣言》，9月2日在東京灣美軍戰艦密蘇里號上簽署投降書，9月9日中國戰區受降，10月25日台灣光復。日本帝國的版圖在幾乎一個月內崩解：海外領土與佔領區全部喪失，南方軍總司令部與各地守軍相繼投降，沖繩的牛島滿與呂相為喜在島上自決，關東軍則因蘇聯參戰而進退失據。日本海軍作為建制的戰爭能力在戰時已被消耗殆盡，聯合艦隊的戰列艦只剩長門一艘，而它也在1945年7月29日被美軍艦隊擊沉；日本本土淪為非戰鬥區並長期被盟軍佔領。太平洋的航線重新被打開，殖民帝國在戰後二十五年內陸續瓦解，這場戰爭的結果最終重塑了二十世紀下半葉的亞洲與全球秩序。
resultEn: The outcome was unconditional Japanese surrender, and the Pacific War ended in complete Allied victory. On 15 August 1945 the Japanese government announced acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration in a rescript of the Emperor; on 2 September the instrument of surrender was signed aboard the American battleship Missouri in Tokyo Bay; the China Theatre received the surrender on 9 September, and Taiwan was recovered on 25 October. The map of the Japanese Empire came apart in the space of little more than a month: every overseas territory and occupied area was lost, the Southern Expeditionary Army Group and the various garrisons surrendered in turn, General Ushijima Mitsuru and Lieutenant General Nishiichi Yōzō on Okinawa took their own lives on the island, and the Kwantung Army was caught between orders as the Soviet Union entered the war. The Japanese Navy as an institution had been spent as a fighting force during the war; of the Combined Fleet's battleships only Nagato remained, and she too was sunk by an American task force on 29 July 1945. The home islands became a non-belligerent zone under long Allied occupation. The Pacific sea lanes were reopened, and the colonial empires broke up one after another within the twenty-five years after the war, so that the result of this conflict reshaped the order of Asia and of the world for the second half of the twentieth century.
